mechanism_narrative: The deceleration in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT recovery seen from t-2w to t-0w (both nearly flat after prior gains) indicates commuting-linked footfall has stopped expanding, which will keep RETAIL_REC flat-to-lower over the next four weeks rather than continuing its earlier rebound.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES moved -16.9 to -16.6 and TRANSIT -28.4 to -29.1 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the last-28-day mean by more than 3 points despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remaining flat or worsening week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week increase in RESIDENTIAL mobility (people spending more time at home) signals renewed caution or reduced discretionary outings, which will suppress RETAIL_REC over the subsequent two weeks if the RESIDENTIAL rise persists beyond a single week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises for two consecutive weeks by more than 0.3 points each week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 6.1 at t-1w to 6.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days even though RESIDENTIAL has risen for two straight weeks, falsifying the caution-driven suppression link.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous stalling of both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT (neither improving by more than 1 point week-on-week) jointly indicates that the commuting-and-errand loop that feeds retail visits has plateaued; the combined stagnation of these two series is a stronger depressive signal for RETAIL_REC than either alone, acting over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT change by less than 1 point in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES changed only 0.3 points and TRANSIT only -0.7 points between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises more than 3 points over the next 4 weeks despite both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remaining within 1 point of their prior week values for multiple consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Large week-to-week swings in PARKS mobility (e.g. 39.7 at t-1w dropping to 16.6 at t-0w) reflect households substituting outdoor recreational trips for retail trips when parks visitation spikes, so a high PARKS reading this week predicts a dip in RETAIL_REC the following week as discretionary time is reallocated.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS swung from -0.7 to 39.7 to 16.6 over the last three weeks while RETAIL_REC stayed roughly flat
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall in the week following a PARKS spike above 30 points in more than half of observed instances.

mechanism_narrative: Under a gradual-reopening regime, the narrowing gap between RETAIL_REC and the already-near-baseline GROCERY_PHARM (essential services) indicates policy easing is extending from essential to non-essential retail, which will continue pulling RETAIL_REC upward toward baseline over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM has hovered near baseline (0.1 to 4.6) while RETAIL_REC improved from -35.7 to -22.0 over the same period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to close further on GROCERY_PHARM's near-baseline level, instead widening the gap or reversing downward over the next 4 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated PARKS mobility driven by favorable seasonal weather diverts discretionary outings away from indoor retail and recreation venues; when the weekly PARKS mean exceeds 20 points, RETAIL_REC growth will stall or reverse in the following one to two weeks as outdoor activity substitutes for shopping trips.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS weekly mean was 25.9 at t-3w and 39.7 at t-1w, both above the 20-point threshold
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise in the two weeks following a PARKS reading above 20, contradicting the proposed substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC's own week-on-week improvement rate has decelerated sharply, from a 10.9-point gain (t-2w to t-1w) to only a 1.4-point loss (t-1w to t-0w); this loss of momentum in the series itself predicts that RETAIL_REC will not resume its earlier rapid recovery pace and will instead average lower over the next four weeks than a naive extrapolation of the earlier trend would suggest.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved by 10.9 points from t-2w to t-1w but worsened by 1.4 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the last-28-day mean by more than 5 points, indicating the deceleration signal was a false negative.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility fails to improve by more than 5 points for two consecutive weeks, it signals that restrictions on public transport use or commuting have hit a policy-imposed floor, which will cap RETAIL_REC recovery over the following two weeks since transit access is a prerequisite for non-local retail visits.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by less than 5 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -28.4 to -29.1 between t-1w and t-0w, a worsening rather than improvement
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises by more than 3 points over the next 14 days despite TRANSIT showing less than 5 points of improvement for two straight weeks.
